proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), let \(\mu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R^d\), and write a randomized rule as \(p=(p_A)_{A\in\mathcal A}\), where each \(p_A\) is a measurable representative, \(p_A\geq0\), and \(\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1\) almost everywhere.  Denote the set of such vectors by \(\mathscr K\).  This representation is legitimate because \(\mathcal A\) is finite.  We first prove the compactness needed for attainment rather than assume it.

For \(j\geq1\), put \(B_j=[-j,j]^d\), and fix a countable orthonormal basis \((e_{jk})_{k\geq1}\) of \(L^2(B_j)\).  Since \(0\leq p_A\leq1\),
\[
 \|p_A\|_{L^2(B_j)}\leq \mu(B_j)^{1/2}. \tag{1}
\]
Given any sequence in \(\mathscr K\), diagonal extraction over the countable triples \((A,j,k)\) makes every coefficient \(\langle p_A,e_{jk}\rangle_{L^2(B_j)}\) converge.  Bessel's inequality and (1) show that the limiting coefficients define an element \(p_A^{(j)}\in L^2(B_j)\), and the extracted sequence converges weakly to it in \(L^2(B_j)\).  Limits on nested boxes agree because every \(L^2(B_j)\) test function, extended by zero, is an \(L^2(B_{j+1})\) test function.  They therefore define a measurable \(p_A\) on \(\mathbb R^d\).  For every nonnegative \(q\in L^2(B_j)\), weak convergence gives \(\int p_Aq\,d\mu\geq0\).  Taking \(q=(p_A)_{-}\) proves \(p_A\geq0\).  Applying the same argument to \(1-p_A\), and testing \(\sum_Ap_A-1\) and its negative part, proves
\[
 0\leq p_A\leq1,
 \qquad \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1
 \quad\text{almost everywhere on every }B_j. \tag{2}
\]
Thus the limit lies in \(\mathscr K\).  The metric obtained by summing the bounded differences of the countably many displayed Fourier coefficients induces the coordinatewise local weak topology on the bounded sets in (1).  The diagonal argument proves sequential compactness in this metric, hence compactness of \(\mathscr K\).

For \(v\in V\), \(h\in D_v\), and \(g\in H_r\), define
\[
 c_{v,h}(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_\Sigma(w-h)
       \sum_{A\ni v}p_A(w)\,dw,
 \qquad
 r_g(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_\Sigma(w-g)
       \sum_A\ell(A)p_A(w)\,dw. \tag{3}
\]
Positive definiteness in \(\text{ass:rational-positive-covariance}\) makes every translated Gaussian density square integrable on each \(B_j\).  Local weak convergence therefore gives convergence of (3) on \(B_j\).  By (2), the absolute contribution off \(B_j\) is at most the corresponding Gaussian tail for \(c_{v,h}\), and at most \(D\) times that tail for \(r_g\).  Letting \(j\to\infty\) proves that every functional in (3) is continuous on \(\mathscr K\).

Consequently
\[
 \mathscr K_\eta=
 \bigcap_{v\in V}\bigcap_{h\in D_v}
 \{p\in\mathscr K:c_{v,h}(p)\geq1-\eta\} \tag{4}
\]
is compact.  It is nonempty because the rule reporting \(V\) surely belongs to it.  The map
\[
 p\longmapsto \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p) \tag{5}
\]
is a supremum of continuous functions and hence is lower semicontinuous.  It attains its minimum on (4).  Gaussian shifts with positive definite covariance are all equivalent to Lebesgue measure, so changing the finitely many coordinates on one common null set turns the minimizer into a measurable Markov kernel valid for every mean.  This proves primal attainment.

We next derive the finite-atomic dual.  Let
\[
 \alpha_v=\sum_{j=1}^{J_v}a_{vj}\delta_{h_{vj}},
 \quad a_{vj}\geq0,quad h_{vj}\in D_v,
 \qquad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^{I}b_i\delta_{g_i},
 \quad b_i\geq0,quad \sum_i b_i=1,quad g_i\in H_r. \tag{6}
\]
Define
\[
 a_v(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,\alpha_v(dh),
 \qquad
 b(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\,\beta(dg). \tag{7}
\]
The Lagrangian associated with the upper-risk epigraph and the coverage inequalities is
\[
 (1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\sum_{A\subseteq V}p_A(w)
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw. \tag{8}
\]
At each \(w\), (2) ranges over a finite action simplex, so pointwise minimization of (8) is attained at a vertex.  Measurability follows by choosing the first minimizing action in a fixed enumeration.  Hence the dual value is exactly
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 =(1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int_{\mathbb R^d}\min_{A\subseteq V}
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw. \tag{9}
\]
For every \(p\in\mathscr K_\eta\), equations (3), (6), and (8) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 &\leq \sum_i b_i r_{g_i}(p)
   +\sum_{v,j}a_{vj}\{(1-\eta)-c_{v,h_{vj}}(p)\}\\
 &\leq \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p).
 \end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
Thus every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate.

It remains to prove that these certificates are exhaustive.  Fix \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The sets
\[
 \{p:r_g(p)>t\},\quad g\in H_r,
 \qquad
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)<1-\eta\},\quad v\in V, h\in D_v, \tag{11}
\]
form an open cover of \(\mathscr K\): an honest rule has supremum risk at least \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)>t\), whereas a nonhonest rule violates one inequality in (4).  Compactness gives a finite subcover with risk points \(g_1,\ldots,g_I\) and coverage points \((v_j,h_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\).  The compact convex set
\[
 Y=\left\{
 \bigl((r_{g_i}(p)-t)_{i\leq I},
 ((1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p))_{j\leq J}\bigr):p\in\mathscr K
 \right\} \tag{12}
\]
is disjoint from the closed negative orthant \(\mathbb R_-^{I+J}\).  To see the sign and strictness of a separator directly, minimize the squared distance between (12) and the negative orthant.  Projection onto that orthant and the two first-order variational inequalities yield a separating normal with nonnegative coordinates.  Disjointness and compactness make the distance positive.  Therefore there are \(\gamma_i,\zeta_j\geq0\), not all zero, and \(q>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\gamma_i\{r_{g_i}(p)-t\}
 +\sum_j\zeta_j\{(1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p)\}
 \geq q
 \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathscr K. \tag{13}
\]
For the rule reporting \(V\), every coverage deficit in (13) equals \(-\eta\).  Hence \(G=\sum_i\gamma_i>0\).  Set \(b_i=\gamma_i/G\) and give the coverage atom \((v_j,h_j)\) mass \(a_j=\zeta_j/G\).  Dividing (13) by \(G\) and taking the infimum over \(p\in\mathscr K\) shows, by (9),
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)\geq t+q/G>t. \tag{14}
\]
Combining (10) and (14), then letting \(t\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), proves
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 =\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ {
m finite\ atomic}}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta). \tag{15}
\]

Finally we prove the asserted effective dense support restriction.  Every \(D_v\) is a finite union of rational polyhedra.  The conditions defining \(H_r\) consist of membership and nonmembership in finitely many such unions and inequalities of the form
\[
 \inf_{x:A x\leq b}(h-x)'\Sigma^{-1}(h-x)\geq r^2. \tag{16}
\]
Introducing the closest-point variable in (16) and eliminating it produces a semialgebraic formula over \(\mathbb Q\); equivalently, one may enumerate the finitely many active sets of the strictly convex quadratic program.  Thus \(D_v\) and \(H_r\) are rational semialgebraic sets.  Enumerate rational open boxes.  Exact sign decomposition of the finitely many defining polynomials decides whether such a box meets the set and, when it does, recursively isolates a real-algebraic sample point: in one variable this is rational root isolation, and in dimension \(k\) one isolates the finitely many real roots in the last coordinate over each sign cell already isolated in dimension \(k-1\).  Every relative neighborhood contains a rational box meeting the set, so the resulting real-algebraic points are dense in each \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\), including zero-dimensional components.

If \(x_n\to x\), then \(\phi_\Sigma(\cdot-x_n)\to\phi_\Sigma(\cdot-x)\) pointwise.  Moreover
\[
 \int|\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n)-\phi_\Sigma(w-x)|\,dw
 =2-2\int\min\{\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n),\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\}\,dw\longrightarrow0, \tag{17}
\]
because the minimum is dominated by \(\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\).  Hence perturbing finitely many support points to the enumerated algebraic points and perturbing their weights to nonnegative rationals, preserving \(\sum_i b_i=1\), makes the mixtures in (7) converge in \(L^1\).  The elementary inequality
\[
 \left|\min_A x_A-\min_A y_A\right|
 \leq\max_A|x_A-y_A| \tag{18}
\]
then shows from (9) that the dual values converge.  Thus rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic supports are dense among all finite atomic certificates.

For completeness, the value of each such certificate is a computable real.  On a rational box, every Gaussian mixture in (7) has computable uniform derivative bounds, so lower and upper Riemann sums for the finite minimum in (9) converge effectively.  Outside the box its absolute value is bounded by \(D b(w)+\sum_va_v(w)\), whose finitely many Gaussian tails have effective outward rational bounds.  Dovetail the support-and-weight enumeration with these two-sided integral enclosures.  Maintain a current certificate and replace it only when the certified lower enclosure of a new candidate exceeds the certified upper enclosure of the current one.  Its exact dual values are nondecreasing.  If its limit were smaller than (15), a candidate separated from that limit by a positive amount would eventually be recognized and would force a replacement.  Therefore the resulting increasing sequence converges upward to (15).  No spatial truncation of the permissible dual support was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\), and \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), for every rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 \max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\longrightarrow0,
\]
with the maximum interpreted as zero when \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}=\varnothing\), and
\[
 \left[B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B\right]^{-1}\longrightarrow
 \Sigma_0.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\psi_j(p)=\alpha_j'p+\beta_j\).  The definition of \(e_{n,j}\) and affinity of \(\psi_j\) give the exact identity
\[
 e_{n,j}(u)=\alpha_j'
 \left(\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right). \tag{1}
\]
Since \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\) is finite, Cauchy--Schwarz and (1) imply
\[
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|
 \leq \left(\max_j\|\alpha_j\|_2\right)
 \sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right\|_2
 \longrightarrow0
\]
by \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\).  If the active set is empty the assertion is immediate.

By \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\) and \(\min_j(p_0)_j\geq\kappa>0\) from \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), every coordinate of \(p_n(0)\) is eventually at least \(\kappa/2\).  Entrywise inversion of the diagonal matrix is then continuous, so
\[
 B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B
 \longrightarrow B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B=I_0. \tag{2}
\]
For \(x\neq0\), full column rank of \(B\) and positivity of \(p_0\) give
\[
 x'I_0x=\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0.
\]
Thus \(I_0\) is positive definite.  Matrix inversion is continuous on the positive-definite cone, and (2), together with the definition \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\), proves the covariance convergence.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Conditional on effective compatibility density, let \(p_n(0)=p_0\), fix a positive-support active stratum and a compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) contained in \(\mathcal U_n\) eventually, and fix a certified rule for \(\mathfrak G_0=\mathfrak G_0(0)\) with Gaussian-null boundaries.  Put
\[
 d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right\|_2.
\]
Carter's recursive experiment-comparison kernel yields \(K_n\) whose semantic-label coverage and diameter-risk discrepancies from their Gaussian counterparts, uniformly over \(u\in C\), are bounded by an explicit remainder depending on \(n,\kappa,C,B,\Sigma_0\), the finite active-facet count, \(d_n(C)\), and \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau)\).  This remainder converges to zero whenever \(d_n(C)\to0\) and then \(\tau\downarrow0\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim says the explicit remainder depends only on \(n,\kappa,C,B,\Sigma_0\) and geometry, but the frozen expansion is qualitative and may converge arbitrarily slowly. Any valid finite-\(n\) bound must expose the realized compact expansion error \(d_n(C)\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Conditional on effective compatibility density and \(\text{ass:effective-moving-remainder}\), suppose \(p_n(0)\to p_0\), \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\), and \(\sup_{u\in C,j}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) for every rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\).  Apply CertGluePFL at a vanishing requested accuracy to the known experiment \(\mathfrak G_0(c_n)\), then transport the certified rule through Carter's positive-cell kernel.  The resulting rule, which uses \(c_n\) but not the unknown limit \(c\), has on each fixed \(C\) a semantic-label coverage deficit and separated-risk excess bounded by Carter's comparison error, \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau_n)\), the displayed moving-remainder charge, covariance and Gaussian-tail enclosures, semantic-union diameter inflation, and \(\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\).  The effective remainder modulus and certificate ledger compute a diagonal choice \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) for which this compact-set bound vanishes.  This statement is a compact-set transfer and does not by itself assert global honesty on every unbounded region \(D_{n,v}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Qualitative convergence of \(e_{n,j}\) cannot compute a diagonal schedule. The existing effective-remainder assumption supplies a modulus, and the conclusion must be identified as compact-set transfer until a separate expanding-domain honesty argument is proved.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Conditional on the effective-compatible-density theorem and \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\), assume \(p_n(0)\to p_0\), \(c_n\to0\), and the compact-uniform local expansion.  Then on every rational compact polytope \(C\), \(\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) and \([B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B]^{-1}\to\Sigma_0\).  Every finite atomic dual certificate for \(\mathfrak G_0\) is contained in a compact local-direction set admitting an eventually lawful multinomial realization, and transfer of that fixed certificate yields \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  Moreover, the required reverse inequality is the existence of one sequence \((K_n)\) with \(K_n\in\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}\) globally on \(D_{n,v}\), obtained from certified zero-offset Gaussian rules by an expanding-domain transfer and exact repair, such that
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{u\in H_{n,r_0}}
 E_{p_n(u)}[\ell_0\{K_n(N_n)\}]
 \leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\]
Consequently \(M_n\to M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  The compact certificate is chosen before the compact set is exhausted; no bounded-support condition is imposed on least-favorable Gaussian dual mass.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The zero-offset target \(\mathfrak G_0\) is not the limit under an unrestricted root-\(n\) base drift. The corrected claim explicitly imposes \(c_n\to0\), records the derived compact-uniform remainder and covariance limits, retains both minimax inequalities, and makes the globally honest expanding-domain primal the unresolved reverse-inequality requirement.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\), the active tangent construction satisfies \(\bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d\).  Every \(u\) fixes a weak sign for each active hyperplane, every zero sign belongs to all incident completions, and exact projection retains a semantic label.  More generally, if \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\) and a compact \(C\) has distance at least \(\tau>0\) from every offset hyperplane \(c_j+a_j'u=0\), then the centered local expansion implies that the lawful sampled-data label on \(C\) eventually equals the label generated by \(D_v^0(c)\).  At \(c=0\) this is the label fan of \(\mathfrak G_0\).  When there are no active cuts, the construction reduces to one global region for the unique retained semantic label, and the honest diameter minimax value is zero.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Compatibility at the single base law does not imply that every direction of \(B\) admits feasible endpoint programs. A local relative-interior condition for the compatible observed-law set is needed before legal optimal branch completions cover all directions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\), the globally completed active tangent arrangement has at least one full-dimensional strict semantic chamber.  The canonical search returns a chamber \(P_{v_*,b_*}^0\), rational \(u_*\), and rational Farkas certificates with \(\rho_0>0\).  For \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\), \(\{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\}\) and \(\inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}\|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\geq r_0\).  Hence \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\) for \(\mathfrak G_0\) without a causal margin assumption.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The strict-chamber conclusion relies on the corrected global-cover premise and therefore must inherit its local compatible-law neighborhood condition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) whose observed law is the rational local base \(p_0=p(P_0)\), and under \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\) for the declared map \(B\), the displayed cell contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures.  The capacity formulas give valid marginal outer bounds, while \(\underline\Delta(t;p_0)\) and \(\overline\Delta(t;p_0)\) are the separate same-law infimum and supremum over \(\mathcal F(p_0)\), attained by \(P_t^-(p_0)\) and \(P_t^+(p_0)\).  Moreover \(\Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)\subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}[\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)]\), with no rectangle-equality claim.  Freezing nonzero base signs and retaining the active directional cuts \(\alpha_\psi'Bu\) yields closed rational cells \(P_{v,b}^0\) covering \(\mathbb R^d\), covariance \(\Sigma_0=\{B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B\}^{-1}\), and a sample-size-free \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\).  This global tangent construction never treats \(p_0+Bu\) as a probability law.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The present statement quantifies an observed law \(p=p(P_0)\) but builds the fan at a separately named \(p_0\). The correction sets \(p_0=p(P_0)\) and states the local compatibility condition needed for a global directional fan.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Assume the declared assignment, positivity, randomization, consistency, no-defier, complier-conditional selection-monotonicity, and aggregate target-mass restrictions.  Let the rational local base satisfy \(p_0=p(P_0)\) for some \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and impose \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\).  For sampled-data transfer also impose multinomial interiority, \(p_n(0)\to p_0\), the centered local expansion, and, for a computable moving-offset schedule, \(\text{ass:effective-moving-remainder}\).  Form \(\mathcal F(p_0)\), compute each same-law coordinate endpoint, form the completed active tangent cells, and certify \(u_*\), \(\rho_0\), and \(r_0\).  Conditional on effective compatibility density, CertGluePFL termination, and the compact-exhaustion transfer theorem, CertGluePFL and exact repair yield one simultaneous \(1-\eta_0\) honest semantic-label rule for every assertion in \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\), an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate Gaussian minimax certificate, and a vanishing sampled-data receipt.  On compact local-direction sets away from active faces, tangent labels equal the eventual lawful multinomial labels.  No rectangular joint identified-set claim is made.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The concrete deliverable must inherit the compatible local-base neighborhood and the effective moving-remainder hypothesis used by its fan and computable transfer schedule.

proposed_assumptions.reason: This is the exact centering condition that makes the zero-offset experiment \(\mathfrak G_0\), rather than a drifted \(\mathfrak G_0(c)\), the candidate local minimax limit.

proposed_assumptions.condition: There exists \(\zeta>0\) such that \(\mathcal F(q)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) satisfying \(\|q-p_0\|_2<\zeta\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: This local relative-interior condition ensures that nearby lawful multinomial laws have nonempty maintained causal fibers. It is stronger than nonemptiness at \(p_0\), but it does not assume any label cover, radius, rule, or minimax conclusion.

proposed.justification: The proposition validates the completed directional fan only on a base having a genuine compatible-law neighborhood.
proposed.gap: Weak-sign bookkeeping is elementary, but feasibility of every symbolic directional endpoint program does not follow from multinomial interiority or a single compatible base law.
proposed.consumer: The corrected cover is required before \(\mathfrak G_0\) can enter the generic experiment class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add a noncircular local relative-interior premise ensuring legal endpoint-program completions in every tangent direction.

proposed.statement: Under \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\), the globally completed active tangent arrangement has at least one full-dimensional strict semantic chamber.  The canonical search returns a chamber \(P_{v_*,b_*}^0\), rational \(u_*\), and rational Farkas certificates with \(\rho_0>0\).  For \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\), \(\{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\}\) and \(\inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}\|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\geq r_0\).  Hence \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\) for \(\mathfrak G_0\) without a causal margin assumption.
proposed.justification: The fixed Gaussian experiment must exhibit a separated point from valid completed tangent geometry.
proposed.gap: The row-distance calculation is complete once a strict legal chamber exists; existence awaits the corrected global-cover premise.
proposed.consumer: The radius receipt verifies the separated-domain condition before certification.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Propagate the corrected cover premise into the strict-chamber and positive-radius claim.

proposed.statement: For every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) whose observed law is the rational local base \(p_0=p(P_0)\), and under \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\) for the declared map \(B\), the displayed cell contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures.  The capacity formulas give valid marginal outer bounds, while \(\underline\Delta(t;p_0)\) and \(\overline\Delta(t;p_0)\) are the separate same-law infimum and supremum over \(\mathcal F(p_0)\), attained by \(P_t^-(p_0)\) and \(P_t^+(p_0)\).  Moreover \(\Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)\subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}[\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)]\), with no rectangle-equality claim.  Freezing nonzero base signs and retaining the active directional cuts \(\alpha_\psi'Bu\) yields closed rational cells \(P_{v,b}^0\) covering \(\mathbb R^d\), covariance \(\Sigma_0=\{B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B\}^{-1}\), and a sample-size-free \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\).  This global tangent construction never treats \(p_0+Bu\) as a probability law.
proposed.justification: The corrected theorem separates same-law causal endpoint identification from the additional local conditions needed to form a global Gaussian label fan.
proposed.gap: The causal fiber and coordinatewise extrema are established, but the global fan still awaits its corrected cover and radius propositions.
proposed.consumer: The Job Corps analysis retains the nonrectangular joint identified set while using coordinatewise endpoint labels at a compatible rational base.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Identify the tangent base with the observed law being analyzed and propagate the local compatible-law neighborhood.

proposed.statement: Assume the declared assignment, positivity, randomization, consistency, no-defier, complier-conditional selection-monotonicity, and aggregate target-mass restrictions.  Let the rational local base satisfy \(p_0=p(P_0)\) for some \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and impose \(\text{ass:local-tangent-fiber-neighborhood}\).  For sampled-data transfer also impose multinomial interiority, \(p_n(0)\to p_0\), the centered local expansion, and, for a computable moving-offset schedule, \(\text{ass:effective-moving-remainder}\).  Form \(\mathcal F(p_0)\), compute each same-law coordinate endpoint, form the completed active tangent cells, and certify \(u_*\), \(\rho_0\), and \(r_0\).  Conditional on effective compatibility density, CertGluePFL termination, and the compact-exhaustion transfer theorem, CertGluePFL and exact repair yield one simultaneous \(1-\eta_0\) honest semantic-label rule for every assertion in \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\), an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate Gaussian minimax certificate, and a vanishing sampled-data receipt.  On compact local-direction sets away from active faces, tangent labels equal the eventual lawful multinomial labels.  No rectangular joint identified-set claim is made.
proposed.justification: This is the concrete causal deliverable, now explicit about the local compatible base and effective moving schedule it needs.
proposed.gap: The causal identification layer is closed, but simultaneous certification and sampled-data minimax equivalence remain downstream of the unresolved global density, termination, and expanding-domain transfer steps.
proposed.consumer: A completed proof would give one replayable multiquantile semantic-label rule without a rectangular joint-set claim.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Propagate the corrected base, fan, and effective moving-schedule premises into the concrete deliverable.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct one nested chart family on the full recession-incidence poset whose weighted edge discrepancies, chart errors, tails, and weight variation vanish simultaneously with an input-computable modulus.
open_obligations.obstruction: The one-chart averaging estimate is conditional on a fixed chart and translation. Independently averaged incident charts need not agree on overlaps, while the weighted gluing inequality only charges the mismatch. No frozen primitive forces or constructs simultaneous compatible choices.
open_obligations.attempted: The prior Gaussian smoothing, covariance-orthogonal quotient, nested tangential boxes, common rational fan, and path telescoping arguments were retained. Their strongest common consequence is the fixed-library ledger, not a uniform incidence modulus.
open_obligations.partial_result: The established smoothing, one-chart averaging, and weighted-gluing inequalities give the respective uniform charges \(R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}\), \(R_fk/(T\sqrt{2\pi})\), and \(\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+R_f\omega(h)/2\).  Hence every fixed chart and every fixed compatible finite library has an explicit ledger.  What is not proved is the existence of one incidence-compatible family whose edge discrepancies vanish simultaneously with an input-computable modulus.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Give total recursive stopping bounds for the unbounded primal search, every weighted Gaussian supremum, cut generation, dual enumeration, and bit precision.
open_obligations.obstruction: Atomic dual convergence and exact coverage repair are now proved, but qualitative candidate density does not identify a finite stage at which all unbounded ledger suprema have outward enclosures and the primal--dual gap is below the requested tolerance.
open_obligations.attempted: Finite rational gridding, active-set linear programming, Gaussian truncation, full-set repair, and dovetailed atomic enumeration close each fixed bounded subproblem. They do not supply the missing global stopping recurrence.
open_obligations.partial_result:
If \(\widetilde K\) has coverage at least \(1-\eta-\rho\), put \(q=\rho/(\eta+\rho)\) and report \(V\) with probability \(q\).  Then
\[
 q+(1-q)(1-\eta-\rho)=1-\eta,
\]
and the risk increases by at most \(Dq=D\rho/(\eta+\rho)\).  The proved atomic-duality theorem supplies sound lower certificates converging to the minimax value.  A complete recursive stage at which all unbounded weighted suprema and the primal--dual gap are simultaneously certified is still missing.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Materialize and adapt a quantitative positive-cell multinomial--Gaussian comparison kernel, with constants and the actual compact expansion error, to semantic coverage and diameter risk.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core contains no theorem-level Carter comparison lemma. Moreover, the current claim omitted the arbitrarily slow model-specific expansion error from its finite-\(n\) remainder.
open_obligations.attempted: The affine-cut identity, compact-uniform remainder convergence, covariance convergence, and away-from-boundary sign stability are proved. These do not bound the distance between the two statistical experiments.
open_obligations.partial_result: For every compact \(C\), the proved remainder lemma gives \(\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) and convergence of the efficient covariance to \(\Sigma_0\).  Consequently, away from a width-\(\tau\) union of active hyperplanes, all finite-sample branch signs equal their zero-offset signs eventually.  The absent step is a theorem-level quantitative multinomial--Gaussian comparison bound, including its dependence on the actual expansion error \(d_n(C)\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: After the effective diagonal is supplied, construct one transferred rule and propagate comparison, boundary, covariance, tail, semantic-union, and ledger charges with exact constants.
open_obligations.obstruction: The effective remainder assumption fixes the noncomputable-diagonal defect, but the quantitative experiment-comparison lemma is absent and compact boundary localization alone does not prove global honesty.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact slack decomposition and univariate Gaussian band bound isolate every sign disagreement on a compact set.
open_obligations.partial_result: If \(|e_{n,j}(u)|<\tau\) and \(|c_{n,j}+a_j'u|>\tau\), then \(\zeta_{n,j}(u)\) and \(c_{n,j}+a_j'u\) have the same sign.  Also \(a_j'W_0\) is univariate normal with variance \(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\), so its density is bounded by \(\{2\pi a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{-1/2}\).  A union bound therefore gives the charged probability \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau)\).  This proves compact boundary localization; it does not construct one globally honest rule on all unbounded finite-sample regions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove both the certificate-first lower transfer and the reverse inequality by constructing one globally honest transferred primal on the expanding lawful multinomial domain.
open_obligations.obstruction: The added zero-offset, compact-remainder, and covariance conditions identify \(\mathfrak G_0\) on every fixed compact. They do not control the experiment or rule on points of \(H_{n,r_0}\) escaping every compact, so reporting the full label set outside a core can raise maximal diameter risk to one.
open_obligations.attempted: Finite dual supports were localized first, and the drift counterexample was removed by \(c_n\to0\). For the upper bound, compact diagonalization and full-set repair were examined, but neither preserves the Gaussian minimax risk on escaping separated means.
open_obligations.partial_result: Under \(c_n\to0\), the compact-uniform expansion, and base convergence, every fixed finite Gaussian dual support has eventually matching zero-offset signs away from a boundary band, and the efficient covariance converges to \(\Sigma_0\).  Thus the certificate-first lower-transfer route is reduced to the missing quantitative experiment comparison.  The reverse inequality remains more demanding: compact-local convergence alone does not control the rule, labels, or experiment comparison on \(H_{n,r_0}\) outside every fixed compact, so no single globally honest expanding-domain primal has yet been constructed.

open_obligations.what_is_open: After adjudication of the proposed local compatible-law neighborhood, prove that every tangent direction admits a legal optimal symbolic completion and hence a semantic cell.
open_obligations.obstruction: Multinomial interiority concerns only observed cell probabilities. Even \(\mathcal F(p_0)\ne\varnothing\) permits \(p_0\) to lie on the boundary of the observable causal model, where some \(Bu\) directions have no feasible endpoint program.
open_obligations.attempted: Weak-sign and equality-face completion proves the cover conditional on existence of one feasible optimal completion at each direction. The proposed relative-interior condition is a model-level, noncircular way to obtain it.
open_obligations.partial_result: Whenever a feasible optimal symbolic completion exists at \(u\), assigning every active cut its weak sign and assigning equality to all incident sides places \(u\) in a completed cell and hence in some \(D_v^0\).  The proposed local relative-interior condition for the compatible observed-law set yields feasible nearby endpoint programs along every direction and is the noncircular route to such a completion.  Without that condition, \(\mathcal F(p_0)\ne\varnothing\) alone need not make an arbitrary direction \(Bu\) tangent to the observable causal model.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish existence of the strict semantic chamber after the corrected cover premise is accepted.
open_obligations.obstruction: The rational row-separation calculation begins only after a legal full-dimensional chamber is known. That existence currently depends on the unresolved corrected global-cover proposition.
open_obligations.attempted: The violated-row Mahalanobis lower bound and positivity of the finite minimum were completed conditionally on a strict chamber.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on a strict semantic chamber and its interior point \(u_*\), every rival component has a violated row with gap \(\gamma>0\).  For every \(g\) in that component, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \geq \gamma/\|A_{i\cdot}^0\|_{\Sigma_0}.
\]
The rational upper enclosure of the denominator makes the recorded \(\rho_{v,b}\) a valid lower distance, and the finite minimum is positive.  Existence of the strict legal chamber remains tied to the unresolved global-cover premise.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Close the corrected fan membership conclusion at the identified base \(p_0=p(P_0)\) after the local-neighborhood, cover, and radius nodes are adjudicated.
open_obligations.obstruction: The same-law endpoint claims are proved, but the frozen theorem used an unrelated \(p_0\), and a compatible base alone does not imply feasibility in every tangent direction.
open_obligations.attempted: Fiber equivalence, coordinatewise endpoint attainment, and the joint-set outer rectangle are complete; the claim was narrowed only in its local-fan hypotheses.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved fiber equivalence and endpoint-attainment propositions imply
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p)
 \subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p),\overline\Delta(t;p)],
\]
and each coordinate endpoint is attained by a single compatible law, separately for that endpoint.  This is an outer rectangle for the joint vector, not a rectangle-equality claim.  The remaining fan conclusion requires identifying the fan base with \(p(P_0)\) and ensuring that every direction of \(B\) has a local compatible-law neighborhood.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Produce the simultaneous globally honest semantic-label rule, the terminating Gaussian certificate, and the vanishing global sampled-data receipt.
open_obligations.obstruction: These outputs consume the unresolved effective incidence modulus, global termination recurrence, corrected fan/radius results, and two-sided expanding-domain transfer.
open_obligations.attempted: The causal fiber, selected-complier contrasts, same-law endpoint witnesses, compact slack localization, and covariance convergence are all available, but none substitutes for the missing global decision-theoretic constructions.
open_obligations.partial_result: The observed instrumental-variable contrasts, the finite response-type polytope, and the same-law endpoint witnesses close the causal identification part under the declared assumptions and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\geq m_*>0\).  They yield coordinatewise sharp effect endpoints and the honest outer inclusion for the joint effect vector.  The simultaneous semantic-label rule and sampled-data minimax interpretation still depend on effective incidence density, terminating global certification, and a globally honest unbounded-domain transfer.

prose_updates.tldr: The exact Gaussian decision value is now proved to attain its globally honest primal optimum and to equal the supremum of finite atomic dual certificates, with rational weights and real-algebraic supports dense without any spatial-support bound. The central effective incidence-density theorem, complete CertGluePFL stopping recurrence, and global Gaussian-to-multinomial transfer remain open. The corrected zero-offset transfer target explicitly requires \(c_n\to0\), compact-uniform moving-remainder convergence, and efficient-covariance convergence, while retaining both \(\liminf M_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) and \(\limsup M_n\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) as the required conclusion.

project_justification.gap: Existing compact decision theory and multinomial--Gaussian comparison do not provide the missing simultaneous rule approximation over an unbounded recession-incidence diagram or a single globally honest expanding-domain transfer. In particular, compact-local convergence of moving slacks does not control separated means escaping every fixed compact.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution currently supplies primal attainment, exact finite-atomic duality, dense rational/algebraic certificate enumeration, Gaussian smoothing, single-chart averaging, weighted path accounting, and exact full-set repair. The remaining program is to construct the effective compatible recession library and then propagate its ledger through a global transferred primal; the zero-offset, remainder, and covariance conditions for that transfer are now explicit.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The local sequence now distinguishes three requirements. Base convergence \(p_n(0)\to p_0\) and the compact-uniform centered expansion imply \(\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) and \([B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B]^{-1}\to\Sigma_0\) on every rational compact \(C\). The zero-offset minimax target additionally requires \(c_n\to0\); a nonzero finite limit instead selects \(\mathfrak G_0(c)\). A computable moving schedule uses the separately declared effective remainder modulus. These compact statements do not by themselves control means escaping to infinity.

prose_updates.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) provides parameter-independent recursive multinomial--Gaussian comparison under positive cells, but the present proof spine still needs its quantitative bound transcribed and adapted to the declared score map, model-specific expansion error, moving faces, and semantic-union loss. Compact Gaussian decision results do not address globally honest rules on an unbounded fan, while drifting-moment-inequality results do not construct the required finite-label minimax transfer. The proved atomic duality here removes any bounded-support premise on least-favorable dual mass; the unresolved novelty is the effective incidence-compatible primal approximation and its global sampled-data transport.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Effective simultaneous incidence density, complete CertGluePFL recurrences, and the milliscale four-label certificate remain open. For sampled-data transfer, \(c_n\to0\), compact-uniform moving-remainder convergence, and covariance convergence identify the zero-offset experiment only on fixed compacts. No proof yet controls the rule and labels on separated means escaping every compact, so the reverse minimax inequality and hence two-sided convergence remain open. The causal fan also needs a compatible observed-law neighborhood, not merely multinomial cell interiority or compatibility at one base point.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Primal attainment and dense finite-atomic duality are unconditional for every encoded experiment in \(\mathfrak E\). Effective density and termination are not claimed proved. The compact-exhaustion theorem retains its two-sided minimax-convergence goal, now under explicit zero-offset, local-remainder, covariance, and compatible-base conditions; the globally honest expanding-domain primal is recorded as the unresolved step rather than replaced by a lower-only result. The causal identified set remains the same-law joint set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp intervals.

statement_notes.justification: The corrected theorem preserves the full two-sided minimax-convergence target and makes every zero-offset limit premise and the required single global primal construction explicit.
statement_notes.gap: Finite atomic duality supports the certificate-first \(\liminf\) route, but compact comparison does not control escaping separated means or deliver the globally honest primal needed for \(\limsup\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).
statement_notes.consumer: Only after both inequalities are proved may the Job Corps archive interpret the Gaussian certificate as the local multinomial minimax benchmark for the identical assertion list.
